usage.callShape: GET https://api.itsgloria.ai/news?feed_categories=ai (x402 pay-per-call; registry surface mislabels it POST — it is actually GET with query params)
usage.outputShape: Response body is a JSON array of news items. Per item: body[].signal (headline), body[].short_context (summary), body[].long_context (detail), body[].sentiment + body[].sentiment_value, body[].feed_categories[], body[].sources[].uri, body[].tokens[] (tickers), body[].tweet_url, body[].timestamp (unix seconds).
quirks: Registry surface lists method=POST, but the real endpoint is GET — call it as GET with query params (inputSchema.type=http method=GET, and probe confirmed GET 402).

feed_categories query param is REQUIRED. It is a comma-separated list from a fixed set: ai, ai_agents, base, bitcoin, crypto, dats, defi, ethereum, hyperliquid, machine_learning, macro, perps, rwa, ripple, solana, tech. Omitting it will fail.
Optional from_date / to_date query params (YYYY-MM-DD) narrow the time window.
Response is a bare JSON array (not wrapped in an object); iterate items directly.
Price is x402 'Varies' — observed $0.03 USDC on Base per call.
usage.guide: Call GET https://api.itsgloria.ai/news with a required feed_categories query param (comma-separated, e.g. feed_categories=ai or feed_categories=crypto,solana) using x402 USDC payment on Base — no API key needed. Despite the registry showing POST, use GET. Optionally add from_date and to_date (YYYY-MM-DD) to bound the window. The response is a JSON array of news items; read each item's .signal for the headline, .short_context / .long_context for the AI summary, .sentiment + .sentiment_value for tone, and .sources[].uri / .tweet_url for links. Cost was ~$0.03 per call.
